A0001.explanation: Abandoned-property content in inspection notice: Include substantially the statutory abandoned-property statement in the written inspection notice. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Use the exact underlying statutory statement: reclaiming abandoned property is conditional, storage and elapsed time may create costs, and prompt contact generally lowers costs. A waiver signed by both parties concerns the 48-hour notice only. It does not waive all security protections or excuse defective content in a notice actually provided. Tenant absence alone is not withdrawal. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Residential security cap: For covered residential security demands or receipts, the ordinary limit is one month of rent, or two months only for a landlord satisfying every small-owner condition and a prospective tenant who is not a service member. First-month rent paid on or before initial occupancy is separately allowed. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Construction year and the address source unit field create no blanket exemption. Reported Units1 is never used as owner-portfolio or building-unit evidence. A pre-July-2024 demand or collection, a qualifying six-month advance, and a specified tenant-requested alteration remain transaction-stage qualifications. An unresolved amount branch does not remove the underlying security protection, and no concrete cap is resolved without an established event and applicable amount conditions. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(a)-(c) [document D025; URL https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1950.5; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Core security accounting: Furnish the core written security accounting. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. State the basis and amount of security received and its disposition; itemize each deduction's amount and purpose. Furnish within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. The $125 and waiver exceptions affect supporting documentation only; they do not excuse the core statement. Use statutory delivery routes: personal delivery or prepaid first-class mail, agreed email or mail arrangements, and controlling multiple-adult arrangements where applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Residential security return; statutory D025 adds precise core timing/delivery and document-specific branches. Return remaining security: Return all security remaining after lawful deductions. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Supporting-document exceptions and estimates do not authorize unrestricted delay of remaining-security return. Use the applicable personal-delivery, prepaid-mailed-check, electronic-payment, written-agreement, or multiple-adult statutory return route. Deduction documentation: Provide the supporting documentation required for security deductions. Provide documents showing incurred repair or cleaning charges, including bills, invoices, or receipts for materials or supplies; provide proof necessary repairs were completed from 2025-01-01. Initial accounting is due within 21 calendar days of vacancy, subject to the qualifying-notice OR 60-days-before-fixed-term-expiration earliest-accounting limit. Only h(2)-(3) documentation may be excused by combined repair-and-cleaning deductions <= $125 OR a tenant-signed waiver substantially including h(2), signed at/after qualifying 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 notice OR no earlier than 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. A tenant request within 14 calendar days after receipt of the statement overrides either exception; comply within 14 calendar days after landlord receipt of the request. A good-faith estimate is permitted if landlord/employee repair cannot reasonably finish within 21 calendar days after vacancy OR outside service/material/supply documents are not in the landlord's possession within that period. Include the estimate with the initial statement; for unavailable outside documents also include provider name, address, and telephone number. Complete accounting and documentation within 14 calendar days after repair completion or document receipt, as applicable. Neither documentation exceptions nor the estimate procedure excuses the independent core statement or remainder return. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Security Deposits [document D007; URL https://rentboard.berkeleyca.gov/rights-responsibilities/security-deposits; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Restoration cost claims: Limit covered materials, supplies and work claims to reasonable necessary restoration costs. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Restoration target is condition at tenancy inception excluding ordinary wear. Preexisting damage or defects and effects of ordinary/cumulative wear across tenancies are not chargeable. Reasonableness and lawful restoration are charge limits, not coverage prerequisites. Performer may affect documentation, not authorization to overcharge. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(a), (e)(2)(A)-(B) [document D025; URL https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1950.5; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Security statement delivery: Furnish the required security itemization through the applicable statement-delivery route. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Default delivery is personal delivery OR prepaid first-class mail. A mutual landlord-tenant agreement at commencement, during, or after tenancy may authorize email to a tenant-provided account OR prepaid first-class mail to a tenant-provided address. For multiple adult tenants residing in the unit, personally deliver or send prepaid first-class mail to one adult selected by the landlord unless a written agreement with the landlord AND all adult tenants specifies refund recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's email or prepaid-mail statement method with corresponding destination. Mail to the tenant-provided address; if none is supplied, mail to the vacated unit. Furnish the statement no later than 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, and no earlier than either party's termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161, OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Electronic refund alone does not authorize email delivery of the statement. Supporting-document exceptions do not excuse this core statement. Conditional residential-rental duty. Event context: Required security itemization, separate from actual refund route. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Offer a complete statutory screening route at collection: At fee collection, offer either the complete process A or the complete process B. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Process A requires ALL: consider completed applications under established screening criteria in receipt order; provide those criteria in writing with the application form; approve the first applicant meeting the criteria; charge no applicant unless or until the application is actually considered. Process A's no-charge condition has a narrow cure only for inadvertent collection caused by multiple concurrent submissions: refund the fee within seven days to an unconsidered applicant, or offer application of the fee to another landlord-offered unit solely at the applicant's discretion. Under A, denial after actual consideration because the applicant fails established criteria does not require a full fee refund. This does not eliminate return of any unused fee portion. Process B requires return of the entire fee to every applicant not selected, regardless of reason, by the earlier of seven days after selection of an applicant or thirty days after application submission. B does not impose A's first-qualified selection policy. A partial combination of the two routes is not a complete statutory alternative. Federal and state housing-assistance-program deposit and fee rules remain applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: State fee context inD005, with fullA/B scope supplied by referenced1950.6. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Security accounting and remainder return: After the tenant vacates, provide the itemized security basis, amount and disposition and return any remainder within 21 calendar days, while respecting the statutory earliest-accounting window. Permitted estimates do not eliminate that core statement and remainder-return duty. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. This accounting duty has no pre-July-2024 security exclusion. The deposit-cap transaction cutoff is not transplanted here. The supporting-document exemptions in (h)(4) do not remove (h)(1); a timely tenant document request can restore the (h)(2)-(3) duties. A repair estimate requires one complete statutory trigger; it is not permission to postpone the entire refund. Follow-up is within 14 calendar days after completion or document receipt. No violation is inferred solely from missing delivery records or the absence of a known move-out event. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(a), (h)(1), (3)-(5) [document D025; URL https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1950.5; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Multiple-adult default refund: Return the remainder by check payable to all adult tenants on the rental or lease agreement at termination. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Residing-adult count determines this regime; the lease roster at termination determines default payees. A complete all-adult written agreement may identify one recipient or divide the remainder with allocation percentages. Divided refunds may use prepaid first-class mailed checks OR electronic deposits to financial accounts designated by each adult as specified in the agreement. A qualifying section 1946.7 termination AND no paragraph (C)(ii) agreement AND a non-joint-check request by the terminating tenant permits, but does not require, a different refund method. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy; no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Multiple adults residing plus remainder/accounting. Multiple-adult statement delivery: Furnish the security itemization under the multiple-adult delivery arrangements. Default: personally deliver or send prepaid first-class mail to one adult tenant selected by the landlord; statement delivery does not depend on a positive remainder. A written agreement made at commencement, during, or after tenancy requires the landlord AND all adult tenants' assent and must specify refund recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's statement method, email or prepaid first-class mail, with corresponding address or account. The section 1946.7 exception changes refund method; it does not independently excuse statement delivery. Furnish within 21 calendar days after vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Ordinary relocation entitlement and annual amount schedule: Pay applicable relocation assistance per unit, using the applicable ordinary or special amount rules. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 ordinary schedule: eligible household $11,000 for tenancy under three years; $14,400 if tenancy is at least three years OR income is at or below 80% AMI. Qualified household corresponding amounts are $23,150 and $27,400. At written termination-notice service, qualified means age at least 62 OR handicapped under Health and Safety Code 50072 OR disabled under 42 USC 423 OR at least one minor dependent child for federal income tax purposes. Otherwise the tenant is eligible. Low income is at or below 80% AMI adjusted for household size regardless of tenure. Listed 2026 limits for household sizes 1–8 are $93,300/$106,600/$119,950/$133,250/$143,900/$154,600/$165,250/$175,900. HUD usually updates in April; exact operative date is absent. Payment is per unit, not per tenant. Pay a sole tenant the entire amount; multiple tenants share equally. If multiple amounts apply, pay the highest. Qualifying owner/family occupancy reductions are $10,550 eligible or $21,250 qualified; qualifying JCO single-family ownership may instead yield one month's rent. These are conditional amount alternatives, not property-wide exemptions. Chart A alone does not determine payment for demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction displacing a household at or below 80% AMI. Assess HCA/RPO enhancement; this does not remove relocation entitlement. An elected Bulletin A accumulated-rent offset is unavailable when relocation is owed because termination is required by a governmental agency order to vacate OR compliance with an issued order for an unpermitted dwelling. Do not assume it applies to distinct HCA/RPO benefits. Amounts increase July 1. Annual rate-selection dates require source review; use neither query date nor notice service automatically. Allocation of owed relocation assistance: Landlord must allocate relocation assistance by unit and among its tenants. Alternative screening-fee processes: At collection of a defined residential application screening fee, offer a fully compliant process A or process B. A combines completed-application receipt order, criteria supplied in writing with the form, first-qualified approval and charging only when considered. A and B are alternatives. Process A considered-denial retention and concurrent-error relief must not be transferred to process B. Application of an inadvertently collected fee to another unit is the applicant's choice; no unilateral credit is authorized. Separate amount, unit availability, unused-fee return, receipt and credit-report-copy duties remain applicable. This plan does not purport to compile every rule in section 1950.6. Take pre-work photographs: Photograph the unit after regaining possession and before deductible repair or cleaning work. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Applies beginning 2025-04-01; the distinct 2025-07-01 new-tenancy photograph threshold is not substituted. Take photographs before the work. Already starting work without photographs is potential noncompliance, not an exclusion. Small deductions and a documentation waiver do not excuse the independent photo-taking duty. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Residential move-out work for deduction; source guide and full D025 document-delivery context. Take post-work photographs: Take after-work photographs required by the reviewed D025 statutory context. The guidance's omission of after-work photographs does not create an exemption from the full statutory duty identified by the reviewed applicability. Supporting-document exceptions do not excuse taking photographs. Deliver photographs and cost explanation: Provide required photographs and a written repair or cleaning cost explanation with the itemization. Deliver photographs and the cost explanation with the security statement; the statutory context additionally includes after-work photographs. Core accounting is due no later than 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, and no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Actual-cost and statutory fee ceilings: Limit each applicant's screening fee to both actual authorized costs and the applicable statutory ceiling. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Fee must be no greater than actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus reasonable owner/agent time value AND no greater than the applicable annual statutory ceiling. Use the lesser of those limits. The statutory base is $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998; that date is not a current dollar amount or original onset of every duty. D005 reports a 2026 ceiling of $68.96; D026 supplies the base and mechanism but not CPI inputs or a computed 2026 maximum. Permission to charge separately requires satisfying the availability restriction AND offering process A OR process B at collection. Process A cumulatively requires receipt-order consideration of completed applications under established criteria, written criteria with the application form, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and charging only upon consideration subject to narrow concurrent-error relief. Concurrent-error relief requires inadvertent collection caused by concurrent submissions and refund to an unconsidered applicant within seven days, or applicant-elected credit to another landlord-offered unit; the seven-day anchor is unspecified. Considered denial for failing criteria alone does not require full refund, but unused-fee return remains. Process B requires the entire fee returned to every unselected applicant regardless of reason by the earlier of selection plus seven days or submission plus 30 days. Failure of permission-to-charge conditions does not remove this fee cap. The fee is neither security under section 1950.5 nor an advance fee under section 10026. Housing-assistance-program provisions are not preempted; express statutory refunds survive the nonrefundable designation. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Fee scope AND fee demand, subject to permission-to-charge gates. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Actor-specific electronic remainder return: Return the remainder electronically through the tenant-authorized destination or method. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Return to a bank or other financial account designated by the tenant in writing OR an electronic or virtual method available to the returning actor and agreed to by the tenant in writing. Prior electronic payment does not itself designate a refund account or establish written consent to a virtual method. For a successor, the former interest must have ended, security must have transferred under subdivision (i), and that successor must personally have received rent electronically; the former landlord's electronic receipts alone do not suffice. A mutual written agreement may designate another return method, including personal delivery or a tenant-payable check sent by prepaid first-class mail to a tenant-provided address. Multiple-adult refunds remain subject to the joint-payee default or a written agreement with landlord AND all adult tenants specifying recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's statement method and destination; divided electronic refunds use accounts designated by each adult. Return within 21 calendar days after vacancy; no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Conditional residential-rental duty. Illegal-occupancy relocation assistance: Landlord must pay relocation assistance for necessary G(3) illegal-occupancy removal. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Assistance equals six times monthly rent; payment is due at least five days before removal and relocation assistance must precede eviction. If payment is not received at least five days before removal AND municipality has established a revolving relocation fund, tenant may receive fund payment and landlord must reimburse the municipality. If no municipal fund exists AND landlord fails timely payment, the unpaid balance bears 18% annual interest until principal and interest are paid in full. The debt is a property lien enforceable by filing a lien statement with county clerk or registrar. Fund availability changes collection route, not base entitlement. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(g) or 2A:18-61.1(h); N.J.A.C. 5:11-8.5(c) [document D067; URL https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_lti/t_i_r.pdf; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:37Z].

Rental advertising protection: Do not publish discriminatory proposed-rental advertisements. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Prohibited grounds: race, creed/religion, color, national origin, sex, gender identity/expression, marital status, civil union status, ancestry, actual or perceived physical or mental disability, nationality, affectional/sexual orientation, familial status, domestic partner status, and lawful income or rent-payment source. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Protection against self-help eviction: Do not force residential occupants out by self-help; physical eviction requires court-officer enforcement after a judge issues a removal warrant. Tenancy survives foreclosure: Continue the residential tenancy after foreclosure; foreclosure alone is not an eviction ground. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Independent lawful eviction grounds remain possible; they do not make foreclosure itself good cause. For a buyer seeking personal primary-residence occupancy, the guide states a 90-day Notice to Quit and no eviction action before a later lease expiration; notice may be given 90 days before lease expiration. The described 90-day protection includes month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units. State or local longer periods and additional protections are not preempted. Voluntary offer and freedom from pressure: Make foreclosure move-out offers in writing and good faith, and preserve the tenant's voluntary choice without pressure. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. A foreclosing agency or new owner may offer money to vacate without establishing good cause; an offer does not authorize involuntary removal. Acceptance is voluntary. No person may misrepresent tenant rights, imply an obligation to accept, threaten consequences for rejection, or harass the tenant. Prohibited pressure includes discontinuing utilities, failing to maintain common areas or facilities or habitable conditions, rent increases exceeding rent-control or leveling limits, and unreasonable or unconscionable increases where rent control does not apply. Writing and good faith are requirements for the offer; oral or bad-faith offers do not escape the protections. New-owner offer notice delivery: The new owner must deliver a separate NOTICE TO TENANTS with the initial and final offers. Delivery applies to initial and final written or verbal offers. This notice is separate from the foreclosing creditor's notice. Acceptance formalities and review period: Record voluntary acceptance in writing with the required receipt-date and review-period acknowledgments. Acceptance must acknowledge the date the offer was received and understanding that the tenant had a five-day period to accept or reject. The five-day period is an offer-review period, not an eviction notice period. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:50-69 et seq.; N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b) [document D067; URL https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_lti/t_i_r.pdf; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:37Z].

Illegal-occupancy relocation assistance: Landlord must pay relocation assistance for necessary G(3) illegal-occupancy removal. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Assistance equals six times monthly rent; payment is due at least five days before removal and relocation assistance must precede eviction. If payment is not received at least five days before removal AND municipality has established a revolving relocation fund, tenant may receive fund payment and landlord must reimburse the municipality. If no municipal fund exists AND landlord fails timely payment, the unpaid balance bears 18% annual interest until principal and interest are paid in full. The debt is a property lien enforceable by filing a lien statement with county clerk or registrar. Fund availability changes collection route, not base entitlement. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(g) or 2A:18-61.1(h); N.J.A.C. 5:11-8.5(c) [document D067; URL https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_lti/t_i_r.pdf; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:37Z].

Rental advertising protection: Do not publish discriminatory proposed-rental advertisements. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Protection against self-help eviction: Do not force residential occupants out by self-help; physical eviction requires court-officer enforcement after a judge issues a removal warrant. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. No small-owner exception is stated. Refusal to allow reentry after police warning about illegal procedures may support disorderly-conduct charges. Successful forcible-entry/detainer action may restore possession and award damages, court costs and reasonable attorney fees; where restoration is inappropriate, the guide states treble damages. Post-eviction removal of belongings must follow Abandoned Property Law. A warrant for removal does not authorize unrelated unlawful retention of belongings. Voluntary offer and freedom from pressure: Make foreclosure move-out offers in writing and good faith, and preserve the tenant's voluntary choice without pressure. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. A foreclosing agency or new owner may offer money to vacate without establishing good cause; an offer does not authorize involuntary removal. Acceptance is voluntary. No person may misrepresent tenant rights, imply an obligation to accept, threaten consequences for rejection, or harass the tenant. Prohibited pressure includes discontinuing utilities, failing to maintain common areas or facilities or habitable conditions, rent increases exceeding rent-control or leveling limits, and unreasonable or unconscionable increases where rent control does not apply. Writing and good faith are requirements for the offer; oral or bad-faith offers do not escape the protections. New-owner offer notice delivery: The new owner must deliver a separate NOTICE TO TENANTS with the initial and final offers. Delivery applies to initial and final written or verbal offers. This notice is separate from the foreclosing creditor's notice. Acceptance formalities and review period: Record voluntary acceptance in writing with the required receipt-date and review-period acknowledgments. Acceptance must acknowledge the date the offer was received and understanding that the tenant had a five-day period to accept or reject. The five-day period is an offer-review period, not an eviction notice period. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:50-69 et seq.; N.J.S.A. 2A:50-71(b) [document D067; URL https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_lti/t_i_r.pdf; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:37Z].

Residential security cap: For covered residential security demands or receipts, the ordinary limit is one month of rent, or two months only for a landlord satisfying every small-owner condition and a prospective tenant who is not a service member. First-month rent paid on or before initial occupancy is separately allowed. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Construction year and the address source unit field create no blanket exemption. Reported Units1 is never used as owner-portfolio or building-unit evidence. A pre-July-2024 demand or collection, a qualifying six-month advance, and a specified tenant-requested alteration remain transaction-stage qualifications. An unresolved amount branch does not remove the underlying security protection, and no concrete cap is resolved without an established event and applicable amount conditions. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5(a)-(c) [document D025; URL https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1950.5; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Core security accounting: Furnish the core written security accounting. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. State the basis and amount of security received and its disposition; itemize each deduction's amount and purpose. Furnish within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. The $125 and waiver exceptions affect supporting documentation only; they do not excuse the core statement. Use statutory delivery routes: personal delivery or prepaid first-class mail, agreed email or mail arrangements, and controlling multiple-adult arrangements where applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Residential security return; statutory D025 adds precise core timing/delivery and document-specific branches. Return remaining security: Return all security remaining after lawful deductions. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Supporting-document exceptions and estimates do not authorize unrestricted delay of remaining-security return. Use the applicable personal-delivery, prepaid-mailed-check, electronic-payment, written-agreement, or multiple-adult statutory return route. Deduction documentation: Provide the supporting documentation required for security deductions. Provide documents showing incurred repair or cleaning charges, including bills, invoices, or receipts for materials or supplies; provide proof necessary repairs were completed from 2025-01-01. Initial accounting is due within 21 calendar days of vacancy, subject to the qualifying-notice OR 60-days-before-fixed-term-expiration earliest-accounting limit. Only h(2)-(3) documentation may be excused by combined repair-and-cleaning deductions <= $125 OR a tenant-signed waiver substantially including h(2), signed at/after qualifying 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 notice OR no earlier than 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. A tenant request within 14 calendar days after receipt of the statement overrides either exception; comply within 14 calendar days after landlord receipt of the request. A good-faith estimate is permitted if landlord/employee repair cannot reasonably finish within 21 calendar days after vacancy OR outside service/material/supply documents are not in the landlord's possession within that period. Include the estimate with the initial statement; for unavailable outside documents also include provider name, address, and telephone number. Complete accounting and documentation within 14 calendar days after repair completion or document receipt, as applicable. Neither documentation exceptions nor the estimate procedure excuses the independent core statement or remainder return. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Security Deposits [document D007; URL https://rentboard.berkeleyca.gov/rights-responsibilities/security-deposits; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

Security statement delivery: Furnish the required security itemization through the applicable statement-delivery route. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Default delivery is personal delivery OR prepaid first-class mail. A mutual landlord-tenant agreement at commencement, during, or after tenancy may authorize email to a tenant-provided account OR prepaid first-class mail to a tenant-provided address. For multiple adult tenants residing in the unit, personally deliver or send prepaid first-class mail to one adult selected by the landlord unless a written agreement with the landlord AND all adult tenants specifies refund recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's email or prepaid-mail statement method with corresponding destination. Mail to the tenant-provided address; if none is supplied, mail to the vacated unit. Furnish the statement no later than 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, and no earlier than either party's termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161, OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Offer a complete statutory screening route at collection: At fee collection, offer either the complete process A or the complete process B. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Process A requires ALL: consider completed applications under established screening criteria in receipt order; provide those criteria in writing with the application form; approve the first applicant meeting the criteria; charge no applicant unless or until the application is actually considered. Process A's no-charge condition has a narrow cure only for inadvertent collection caused by multiple concurrent submissions: refund the fee within seven days to an unconsidered applicant, or offer application of the fee to another landlord-offered unit solely at the applicant's discretion. Under A, denial after actual consideration because the applicant fails established criteria does not require a full fee refund. This does not eliminate return of any unused fee portion. Process B requires return of the entire fee to every applicant not selected, regardless of reason, by the earlier of seven days after selection of an applicant or thirty days after application submission. B does not impose A's first-qualified selection policy. A partial combination of the two routes is not a complete statutory alternative. Federal and state housing-assistance-program deposit and fee rules remain applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: State fee context inD005, with fullA/B scope supplied by referenced1950.6. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Multiple-adult default refund: Return the remainder by check payable to all adult tenants on the rental or lease agreement at termination. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Residing-adult count determines this regime; the lease roster at termination determines default payees. A complete all-adult written agreement may identify one recipient or divide the remainder with allocation percentages. Divided refunds may use prepaid first-class mailed checks OR electronic deposits to financial accounts designated by each adult as specified in the agreement. A qualifying section 1946.7 termination AND no paragraph (C)(ii) agreement AND a non-joint-check request by the terminating tenant permits, but does not require, a different refund method. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy; no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Multiple adults residing plus remainder/accounting. Multiple-adult statement delivery: Furnish the security itemization under the multiple-adult delivery arrangements. Default: personally deliver or send prepaid first-class mail to one adult tenant selected by the landlord; statement delivery does not depend on a positive remainder. A written agreement made at commencement, during, or after tenancy requires the landlord AND all adult tenants' assent and must specify refund recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's statement method, email or prepaid first-class mail, with corresponding address or account. The section 1946.7 exception changes refund method; it does not independently excuse statement delivery. Furnish within 21 calendar days after vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Ordinary relocation entitlement and annual amount schedule: Pay applicable relocation assistance per unit, using the applicable ordinary or special amount rules. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 ordinary schedule: eligible household $11,000 for tenancy under three years; $14,400 if tenancy is at least three years OR income is at or below 80% AMI. Qualified household corresponding amounts are $23,150 and $27,400. At written termination-notice service, qualified means age at least 62 OR handicapped under Health and Safety Code 50072 OR disabled under 42 USC 423 OR at least one minor dependent child for federal income tax purposes. Otherwise the tenant is eligible. Low income is at or below 80% AMI adjusted for household size regardless of tenure. Listed 2026 limits for household sizes 1–8 are $93,300/$106,600/$119,950/$133,250/$143,900/$154,600/$165,250/$175,900. HUD usually updates in April; exact operative date is absent. Payment is per unit, not per tenant. Pay a sole tenant the entire amount; multiple tenants share equally. If multiple amounts apply, pay the highest. Qualifying owner/family occupancy reductions are $10,550 eligible or $21,250 qualified; qualifying JCO single-family ownership may instead yield one month's rent. These are conditional amount alternatives, not property-wide exemptions. Chart A alone does not determine payment for demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction displacing a household at or below 80% AMI. Assess HCA/RPO enhancement; this does not remove relocation entitlement. An elected Bulletin A accumulated-rent offset is unavailable when relocation is owed because termination is required by a governmental agency order to vacate OR compliance with an issued order for an unpermitted dwelling. Do not assume it applies to distinct HCA/RPO benefits. Amounts increase July 1. Annual rate-selection dates require source review; use neither query date nor notice service automatically. Actual-cost and statutory fee ceilings: Limit each applicant's screening fee to both actual authorized costs and the applicable statutory ceiling. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Fee must be no greater than actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus reasonable owner/agent time value AND no greater than the applicable annual statutory ceiling. Use the lesser of those limits. The statutory base is $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998; that date is not a current dollar amount or original onset of every duty. D005 reports a 2026 ceiling of $68.96; D026 supplies the base and mechanism but not CPI inputs or a computed 2026 maximum. Permission to charge separately requires satisfying the availability restriction AND offering process A OR process B at collection. Process A cumulatively requires receipt-order consideration of completed applications under established criteria, written criteria with the application form, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and charging only upon consideration subject to narrow concurrent-error relief. Concurrent-error relief requires inadvertent collection caused by concurrent submissions and refund to an unconsidered applicant within seven days, or applicant-elected credit to another landlord-offered unit; the seven-day anchor is unspecified. Considered denial for failing criteria alone does not require full refund, but unused-fee return remains. Process B requires the entire fee returned to every unselected applicant regardless of reason by the earlier of selection plus seven days or submission plus 30 days. Failure of permission-to-charge conditions does not remove this fee cap. The fee is neither security under section 1950.5 nor an advance fee under section 10026. Housing-assistance-program provisions are not preempted; express statutory refunds survive the nonrefundable designation. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Fee scope AND fee demand, subject to permission-to-charge gates. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Limits on security claims: Limit security claims to reasonably necessary amounts for statutory purposes. Actor-specific electronic remainder return: Return the remainder electronically through the tenant-authorized destination or method. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Return to a bank or other financial account designated by the tenant in writing OR an electronic or virtual method available to the returning actor and agreed to by the tenant in writing. Prior electronic payment does not itself designate a refund account or establish written consent to a virtual method. For a successor, the former interest must have ended, security must have transferred under subdivision (i), and that successor must personally have received rent electronically; the former landlord's electronic receipts alone do not suffice. A mutual written agreement may designate another return method, including personal delivery or a tenant-payable check sent by prepaid first-class mail to a tenant-provided address. Multiple-adult refunds remain subject to the joint-payee default or a written agreement with landlord AND all adult tenants specifying recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's statement method and destination; divided electronic refunds use accounts designated by each adult. Return within 21 calendar days after vacancy; no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Core security accounting: Furnish the core written security accounting. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. State the basis and amount of security received and its disposition; itemize each deduction's amount and purpose. Furnish within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. The $125 and waiver exceptions affect supporting documentation only; they do not excuse the core statement. Use statutory delivery routes: personal delivery or prepaid first-class mail, agreed email or mail arrangements, and controlling multiple-adult arrangements where applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. Return remaining security: Return all security remaining after lawful deductions. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Supporting-document exceptions and estimates do not authorize unrestricted delay of remaining-security return. Use the applicable personal-delivery, prepaid-mailed-check, electronic-payment, written-agreement, or multiple-adult statutory return route. Deduction documentation: Provide the supporting documentation required for security deductions. Provide documents showing incurred repair or cleaning charges, including bills, invoices, or receipts for materials or supplies; provide proof necessary repairs were completed from 2025-01-01. Initial accounting is due within 21 calendar days of vacancy, subject to the qualifying-notice OR 60-days-before-fixed-term-expiration earliest-accounting limit. Only h(2)-(3) documentation may be excused by combined repair-and-cleaning deductions <= $125 OR a tenant-signed waiver substantially including h(2), signed at/after qualifying 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 notice OR no earlier than 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. A tenant request within 14 calendar days after receipt of the statement overrides either exception; comply within 14 calendar days after landlord receipt of the request. A good-faith estimate is permitted if landlord/employee repair cannot reasonably finish within 21 calendar days after vacancy OR outside service/material/supply documents are not in the landlord's possession within that period. Include the estimate with the initial statement; for unavailable outside documents also include provider name, address, and telephone number. Complete accounting and documentation within 14 calendar days after repair completion or document receipt, as applicable. Neither documentation exceptions nor the estimate procedure excuses the independent core statement or remainder return. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Offer a complete statutory screening route at collection: At fee collection, offer either the complete process A or the complete process B. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Process A requires ALL: consider completed applications under established screening criteria in receipt order; provide those criteria in writing with the application form; approve the first applicant meeting the criteria; charge no applicant unless or until the application is actually considered. Process A's no-charge condition has a narrow cure only for inadvertent collection caused by multiple concurrent submissions: refund the fee within seven days to an unconsidered applicant, or offer application of the fee to another landlord-offered unit solely at the applicant's discretion. Under A, denial after actual consideration because the applicant fails established criteria does not require a full fee refund. This does not eliminate return of any unused fee portion. Process B requires return of the entire fee to every applicant not selected, regardless of reason, by the earlier of seven days after selection of an applicant or thirty days after application submission. B does not impose A's first-qualified selection policy. A partial combination of the two routes is not a complete statutory alternative. Federal and state housing-assistance-program deposit and fee rules remain applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Alternative screening-fee processes: At collection of a defined residential application screening fee, offer a fully compliant process A or process B. A combines completed-application receipt order, criteria supplied in writing with the form, first-qualified approval and charging only when considered. B requires full refunds to all unselected applicants by the earlier statutory deadline. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. A and B are alternatives. Process A considered-denial retention and concurrent-error relief must not be transferred to process B. Application of an inadvertently collected fee to another unit is the applicant's choice; no unilateral credit is authorized. Separate amount, unit availability, unused-fee return, receipt and credit-report-copy duties remain applicable. This plan does not purport to compile every rule in section 1950.6. No specific 2026 annual amount is encoded in this rule because its own source gives the adjustable base rather than the needed CPI observations. Ordinary default remainder-return route: Return remaining security by personal delivery OR a check payable to the tenant sent by prepaid first-class mail. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Mail to the tenant-provided address; if none was supplied, use the vacated unit. Return no later than 21 calendar days after actual vacancy and no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Under the electronic regime, a written landlord-tenant agreement may designate another route, including personal delivery or mailed check; such a route derives from the agreement rather than this ordinary default. A section 1946.7 departure additionally requires qualifying termination, no paragraph (C)(ii) agreement, and a non-joint-check request by that terminating tenant. Conditional residential-rental duty. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Beginning April 1, 2025, take photographs within a reasonable time after possession returns and before repairs or cleaning supporting a security deduction or claim. Deductions and claims must be allowed by the section; unlawful claims do not excuse missing photographs. Subdivision (h) small-charge and waiver documentation exceptions do not expressly eliminate this independent subdivision (g) duty. Conditional residential-rental duty. Beginning April 1, 2025, take photographs within a reasonable time after completion. The post-work duty does not depend on compliance with the pre-work photograph duty. Claims remain subject to the section's deduction restrictions. Subdivision (h) documentation exceptions do not expressly eliminate photograph-taking. Schedule and perform the requested inspection: Attempt mutually acceptable scheduling and perform the requested initial inspection. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Inspect at a reasonable time, no earlier than two weeks before termination or lease end, and before any final inspection after vacancy. Attempt to agree on date and time; lack of agreement is not itself a blanket exemption. Proceed whether or not the tenant is present unless the tenant previously withdrew the request. A signed 48-hour notice waiver does not waive the inspection duty. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Requested, nonwithdrawn initial inspection under shared scope. Written appointment notice: Give written notice of the inspection date and time at least 48 hours beforehand. Notice is required if a mutual time is agreed OR if agreement cannot be reached and the tenant still wants inspection. Both-party signed written waiver affects only the 48-hour notice. Tenant absence alone does not cancel the inspection. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Written inspection-option notice: Notify the tenant in writing of the option to request an initial inspection and the right to be present. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Notify within a reasonable time after either party communicates intention to terminate, or before lease-term end. No inspection request, or later withdrawal, does not erase this preceding notice duty. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Applicable residential termination/inspection procedure. Perform requested initial inspection: Perform the requested initial inspection to identify repair or cleaning deficiencies and allow correction before security deductions. Inspect at a reasonable time no earlier than two weeks before termination or lease end, before any final post-vacancy inspection. Attempt mutually acceptable scheduling. Give at least 48 hours' prior written appointment notice if a mutual time is agreed OR no mutual time is possible but tenant still wants inspection. Only a written waiver signed by both landlord and tenant dispenses with this appointment notice. Proceed regardless of tenant attendance unless the tenant previously withdrew the request. After notice of the option, choosing not to request discharges subsequent inspection duties. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Disposition when landlord interest ends: Landlord or agent must dispose of remaining security within a reasonable time after the landlord's interest ends. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. End of interest includes sale, assignment, death, appointment of receiver or otherwise; a manager change alone does not establish this event. Complete either alternative: transfer the remainder after lawful subdivision (e) deductions to the successor AND provide the subdivision (i)(1) notice; OR return the lawful remainder to the tenant AND provide subdivision (h) accounting. Transfer notice must be personally delivered OR sent by prepaid first-class mail and disclose transfer, claims, deposited amount, and successors' names, addresses and telephone numbers. Personal delivery requires tenant acknowledgment and signature on the landlord's copy. Either complete compliant alternative releases further liability for the held security. Performance and release are compliance consequences, not prerequisites to the disposition duty. Reasonable time has no supplied numeric deadline. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Actual-cost and statutory fee ceilings: Limit each applicant's screening fee to both actual authorized costs and the applicable statutory ceiling. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Fee must be no greater than actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus reasonable owner/agent time value AND no greater than the applicable annual statutory ceiling. Use the lesser of those limits. The statutory base is $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998; that date is not a current dollar amount or original onset of every duty. D005 reports a 2026 ceiling of $68.96; D026 supplies the base and mechanism but not CPI inputs or a computed 2026 maximum. Permission to charge separately requires satisfying the availability restriction AND offering process A OR process B at collection. Process A cumulatively requires receipt-order consideration of completed applications under established criteria, written criteria with the application form, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and charging only upon consideration subject to narrow concurrent-error relief. Concurrent-error relief requires inadvertent collection caused by concurrent submissions and refund to an unconsidered applicant within seven days, or applicant-elected credit to another landlord-offered unit; the seven-day anchor is unspecified. Considered denial for failing criteria alone does not require full refund, but unused-fee return remains. Process B requires the entire fee returned to every unselected applicant regardless of reason by the earlier of selection plus seven days or submission plus 30 days. Failure of permission-to-charge conditions does not remove this fee cap. The fee is neither security under section 1950.5 nor an advance fee under section 10026. Housing-assistance-program provisions are not preempted; express statutory refunds survive the nonrefundable designation. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Fee scope AND fee demand, subject to permission-to-charge gates. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Actor-specific electronic remainder return: Return the remainder electronically through the tenant-authorized destination or method. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Return to a bank or other financial account designated by the tenant in writing OR an electronic or virtual method available to the returning actor and agreed to by the tenant in writing. Prior electronic payment does not itself designate a refund account or establish written consent to a virtual method. For a successor, the former interest must have ended, security must have transferred under subdivision (i), and that successor must personally have received rent electronically; the former landlord's electronic receipts alone do not suffice. A mutual written agreement may designate another return method, including personal delivery or a tenant-payable check sent by prepaid first-class mail to a tenant-provided address. Multiple-adult refunds remain subject to the joint-payee default or a written agreement with landlord AND all adult tenants specifying recipients, allocation percentages if divided, refund route, and each adult's statement method and destination; divided electronic refunds use accounts designated by each adult. Return within 21 calendar days after vacancy; no earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Conditional residential-rental duty. Six-month notice presumption: Apply a rebuttable presumption of reprisal to a qualifying notice received within six months after qualifying activity. Core security accounting: Furnish the core written security accounting. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. State the basis and amount of security received and its disposition; itemize each deduction's amount and purpose. Furnish within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying termination notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. The $125 and waiver exceptions affect supporting documentation only; they do not excuse the core statement. Use statutory delivery routes: personal delivery or prepaid first-class mail, agreed email or mail arrangements, and controlling multiple-adult arrangements where applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. Return remaining security: Return all security remaining after lawful deductions. Return within 21 calendar days after actual vacancy, but not earlier than qualifying notice under 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 OR 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. Supporting-document exceptions and estimates do not authorize unrestricted delay of remaining-security return. Use the applicable personal-delivery, prepaid-mailed-check, electronic-payment, written-agreement, or multiple-adult statutory return route. Deduction documentation: Provide the supporting documentation required for security deductions. Provide documents showing incurred repair or cleaning charges, including bills, invoices, or receipts for materials or supplies; provide proof necessary repairs were completed from 2025-01-01. Initial accounting is due within 21 calendar days of vacancy, subject to the qualifying-notice OR 60-days-before-fixed-term-expiration earliest-accounting limit. Only h(2)-(3) documentation may be excused by combined repair-and-cleaning deductions <= $125 OR a tenant-signed waiver substantially including h(2), signed at/after qualifying 1946, 1946.1, or CCP1161 notice OR no earlier than 60 calendar days before fixed-term expiration. A tenant request within 14 calendar days after receipt of the statement overrides either exception; comply within 14 calendar days after landlord receipt of the request. A good-faith estimate is permitted if landlord/employee repair cannot reasonably finish within 21 calendar days after vacancy OR outside service/material/supply documents are not in the landlord's possession within that period. Include the estimate with the initial statement; for unavailable outside documents also include provider name, address, and telephone number. Neither documentation exceptions nor the estimate procedure excuses the independent core statement or remainder return. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Offer a complete statutory screening route at collection: At fee collection, offer either the complete process A or the complete process B. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Process A requires ALL: consider completed applications under established screening criteria in receipt order; provide those criteria in writing with the application form; approve the first applicant meeting the criteria; charge no applicant unless or until the application is actually considered. Process A's no-charge condition has a narrow cure only for inadvertent collection caused by multiple concurrent submissions: refund the fee within seven days to an unconsidered applicant, or offer application of the fee to another landlord-offered unit solely at the applicant's discretion. Under A, denial after actual consideration because the applicant fails established criteria does not require a full fee refund. This does not eliminate return of any unused fee portion. Process B requires return of the entire fee to every applicant not selected, regardless of reason, by the earlier of seven days after selection of an applicant or thirty days after application submission. B does not impose A's first-qualified selection policy. A partial combination of the two routes is not a complete statutory alternative. Federal and state housing-assistance-program deposit and fee rules remain applicable. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Ordinary relocation entitlement and annual amount schedule: Pay applicable relocation assistance per unit, using the applicable ordinary or special amount rules. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. July 1, 2026–June 30, 2027 ordinary schedule: eligible household $11,000 for tenancy under three years; $14,400 if tenancy is at least three years OR income is at or below 80% AMI. Qualified household corresponding amounts are $23,150 and $27,400. At written termination-notice service, qualified means age at least 62 OR handicapped under Health and Safety Code 50072 OR disabled under 42 USC 423 OR at least one minor dependent child for federal income tax purposes. Otherwise the tenant is eligible. Low income is at or below 80% AMI adjusted for household size regardless of tenure. Listed 2026 limits for household sizes 1–8 are $93,300/$106,600/$119,950/$133,250/$143,900/$154,600/$165,250/$175,900. HUD usually updates in April; exact operative date is absent. Payment is per unit, not per tenant. Pay a sole tenant the entire amount; multiple tenants share equally. If multiple amounts apply, pay the highest. Qualifying owner/family occupancy reductions are $10,550 eligible or $21,250 qualified; qualifying JCO single-family ownership may instead yield one month's rent. These are conditional amount alternatives, not property-wide exemptions. Chart A alone does not determine payment for demolition of a Protected Unit for new construction displacing a household at or below 80% AMI. Assess HCA/RPO enhancement; this does not remove relocation entitlement. An elected Bulletin A accumulated-rent offset is unavailable when relocation is owed because termination is required by a governmental agency order to vacate OR compliance with an issued order for an unpermitted dwelling. Do not assume it applies to distinct HCA/RPO benefits. Amounts increase July 1. Annual rate-selection dates require source review; use neither query date nor notice service automatically. Relevant source conflict: Detailed reduced-payment conditions and Chart A specify owner/family occupancy, while another sentence includes manager occupancy; reduced schedule eligibility is unresolved.. Allocation of owed relocation assistance: Landlord must allocate relocation assistance by unit and among its tenants. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. If exactly one tenant occupies the unit, pay that tenant the entire unit payment. If two or more tenants occupy the unit, pay each an equal pro rata share. If multiple payment amounts apply, pay the highest applicable amount for the unit; do not sum separate unit awards. Tenant count means tenants occupying this unit, not household size or building units. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: A. Alternative screening-fee processes: At collection of a defined residential application screening fee, offer a fully compliant process A or process B. A combines completed-application receipt order, criteria supplied in writing with the form, first-qualified approval and charging only when considered. B requires full refunds to all unselected applicants by the earlier statutory deadline. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. A and B are alternatives. Process A considered-denial retention and concurrent-error relief must not be transferred to process B. Application of an inadvertently collected fee to another unit is the applicant's choice; no unilateral credit is authorized. Separate amount, unit availability, unused-fee return, receipt and credit-report-copy duties remain applicable. This plan does not purport to compile every rule in section 1950.6. No specific 2026 annual amount is encoded in this rule because its own source gives the adjustable base rather than the needed CPI observations. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.6(a)-(c), (e), (h)-(l) [document D026; URL https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=1950.6; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:35Z].

A signed 48-hour notice waiver does not waive the inspection duty. Conditional residential-rental duty. Disposition when landlord interest ends: Landlord or agent must dispose of remaining security within a reasonable time after the landlord's interest ends. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. End of interest includes sale, assignment, death, appointment of receiver or otherwise; a manager change alone does not establish this event. Complete either alternative: transfer the remainder after lawful subdivision (e) deductions to the successor AND provide the subdivision (i)(1) notice; OR return the lawful remainder to the tenant AND provide subdivision (h) accounting. Transfer notice must be personally delivered OR sent by prepaid first-class mail and disclose transfer, claims, deposited amount, and successors' names, addresses and telephone numbers. Personal delivery requires tenant acknowledgment and signature on the landlord's copy. Either complete compliant alternative releases further liability for the held security. Performance and release are compliance consequences, not prerequisites to the disposition duty. Reasonable time has no supplied numeric deadline. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Actual-cost and statutory fee ceilings: Limit each applicant's screening fee to both actual authorized costs and the applicable statutory ceiling. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Fee must be no greater than actual out-of-pocket information-gathering costs plus reasonable owner/agent time value AND no greater than the applicable annual statutory ceiling. Use the lesser of those limits. The statutory base is $30 per applicant, adjustable annually commensurate with CPI increases beginning January 1, 1998; that date is not a current dollar amount or original onset of every duty. D005 reports a 2026 ceiling of $68.96; D026 supplies the base and mechanism but not CPI inputs or a computed 2026 maximum. Permission to charge separately requires satisfying the availability restriction AND offering process A OR process B at collection. Process A cumulatively requires receipt-order consideration of completed applications under established criteria, written criteria with the application form, approval of the first qualifying applicant, and charging only upon consideration subject to narrow concurrent-error relief. Concurrent-error relief requires inadvertent collection caused by concurrent submissions and refund to an unconsidered applicant within seven days, or applicant-elected credit to another landlord-offered unit; the seven-day anchor is unspecified. Considered denial for failing criteria alone does not require full refund, but unused-fee return remains. Process B requires the entire fee returned to every unselected applicant regardless of reason by the earlier of selection plus seven days or submission plus 30 days. Failure of permission-to-charge conditions does not remove this fee cap. The fee is neither security under section 1950.5 nor an advance fee under section 10026. Housing-assistance-program provisions are not preempted; express statutory refunds survive the nonrefundable designation. Conditional residential-rental duty. The payment definition, actual event, event-date version, procedural prerequisites and exceptions remain necessary for the event result; coverage alone establishes none of them. Event context: Fee scope AND fee demand, subject to permission-to-charge gates. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Cal. Civ. Illegal-occupancy relocation assistance: Landlord must pay relocation assistance for necessary G(3) illegal-occupancy removal. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Assistance equals six times monthly rent; payment is due at least five days before removal and relocation assistance must precede eviction. If payment is not received at least five days before removal AND municipality has established a revolving relocation fund, tenant may receive fund payment and landlord must reimburse the municipality. If no municipal fund exists AND landlord fails timely payment, the unpaid balance bears 18% annual interest until principal and interest are paid in full. The debt is a property lien enforceable by filing a lien statement with county clerk or registrar. Fund availability changes collection route, not base entitlement. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(g) or 2A:18-61.1(h); N.J.A.C. 5:11-8.5(c) [document D067; URL https://www.nj.gov/dca/codes/publications/pdf_lti/t_i_r.pdf; retrieved 2026-10-01T22:37Z].

Rental advertising protection: Do not publish discriminatory proposed-rental advertisements. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Prohibited grounds: race, creed/religion, color, national origin, sex, gender identity/expression, marital status, civil union status, ancestry, actual or perceived physical or mental disability, nationality, affectional/sexual orientation, familial status, domestic partner status, and lawful income or rent-payment source. Familial status includes families with children under 18 and pregnant women; disability includes AIDS/HIV and perceived AIDS. Evaluate each challenged ground separately; a familial-status or religious allowance does not authorize other discrimination. Discriminatory content is a compliance issue; a compliant published rental advertisement remains subject to the prohibition. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Protection against self-help eviction: Do not force residential occupants out by self-help; physical eviction requires court-officer enforcement after a judge issues a removal warrant. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. No small-owner exception is stated. Refusal to allow reentry after police warning about illegal procedures may support disorderly-conduct charges. Successful forcible-entry/detainer action may restore possession and award damages, court costs and reasonable attorney fees; where restoration is inappropriate, the guide states treble damages. Post-eviction removal of belongings must follow Abandoned Property Law. A warrant for removal does not authorize unrelated unlawful retention of belongings. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Tenancy survives foreclosure: Continue the residential tenancy after foreclosure; foreclosure alone is not an eviction ground. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. Independent lawful eviction grounds remain possible; they do not make foreclosure itself good cause. For a buyer seeking personal primary-residence occupancy, the guide states a 90-day Notice to Quit and no eviction action before a later lease expiration; notice may be given 90 days before lease expiration. The described 90-day protection includes month-to-month tenants and owner-occupied two- and three-family units. State or local longer periods and additional protections are not preempted. The separate federal notice discussion is not compiled as a distinct state permission or obligation; its full authority and eligibility require review. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed. Citation: Chase Manhattan Bank v. Voluntary offer and freedom from pressure: Make foreclosure move-out offers in writing and good faith, and preserve the tenant's voluntary choice without pressure. This is a governing conditional protection; the event and event-specific exclusions are not established. A foreclosing agency or new owner may offer money to vacate without establishing good cause; an offer does not authorize involuntary removal. Acceptance is voluntary. No person may misrepresent tenant rights, imply an obligation to accept, threaten consequences for rejection, or harass the tenant. Prohibited pressure includes discontinuing utilities, failing to maintain common areas or facilities or habitable conditions, rent increases exceeding rent-control or leveling limits, and unreasonable or unconscionable increases where rent control does not apply. Writing and good faith are requirements for the offer; oral or bad-faith offers do not escape the protections. New-owner offer notice delivery: The new owner must deliver a separate NOTICE TO TENANTS with the initial and final offers. Delivery applies to initial and final written or verbal offers. This notice is separate from the foreclosing creditor's notice. Acceptance formalities and review period: Record voluntary acceptance in writing with the required receipt-date and review-period acknowledgments. Acceptance must acknowledge the date the offer was received and understanding that the tenant had a five-day period to accept or reject. The five-day period is an offer-review period, not an eviction notice period. Coverage does not establish compliance, violation, or an amount currently owed.
